lines: Morgan Kim
+1 (555) 010-8173 | morgan.kim@example.com | example.com/code/mkim
EDUCATION
Clearwater Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2017 - May 2021
EXPERIENCE
Voltline Robotics | Embedded Software Engineer | Metro City, USA | Mar 2023 - Jun 2025
- Improved update speed by 60% by compressing firmware images and resuming interrupted downloads.
- Wrote a hardware-in-the-loop test rig that ran 400 motor-control tests on every firmware build.
- Added a crash logger that saved the last 2 seconds of sensor data to flash, which found the root cause of 5 field failures.
- Sampled the motor's 5 kHz vibration signal at 8 kHz so the fault detector could capture it without aliasing.
- Fixed a race condition on the counter shared by the interrupt handler and the main loop by declaring the counter volatile.
- Rewrote the motor-controller firmware for a warehouse robot fleet of 300 units, cutting control-loop jitter from 120 to 15 microseconds and field motor faults by 60%.
Clearwater Sensors | Hardware Test Engineer | Metro City, USA | Apr 2022 - Feb 2023
- Automated end-of-line tests for a humidity sensor, cutting test time per unit from 90 to 25 seconds across 20,000 units a month.
- Traced a batch of early field failures to a solder-paste change; the findings updated the reflow profile and cut returns from 2.1% to 0.4%.
- Wrote the calibration procedure for the sensor line, cutting calibration drift complaints from 15 to 2 a quarter.
- Designed a test fixture that checked 8 boards at once, raising station throughput from 40 to 150 boards an hour.
PROJECTS
Low-Power Weather Station | Independent Project | C, STM32 | Jan 2025 - Present
- Engineered a next-generation, innovation-driven IoT solution that redefines sustainable environmental sensing.
- Cut average current from 4.2 mA to 0.9 mA by sleeping between readings and batching radio transmissions.
- Published the schematics and firmware openly, and a local school built two stations from them.
Formula Student Electric Car | Electronics Lead, Team of 12 | C | Sep 2019 - May 2021
- Worked on firmware and testing for the robot fleet's motor controllers.
- The CAN-bus firmware for the dashboard was written and tested against the motor controller before each race.
- Rewrote motor-control firmware for a fleet of about 300 robots, cutting control-loop jitter eightfold and motor faults by more than half.
SKILLS
Tools: C, C++, STM32, oscilloscopes, FPGA
Methods: firmware, hardware-in-the-loop testing, CAN, low-power design

items.says: Make the code link lead directly to work an employer should inspect.
Use a complete, working URL if this is a real résumé.
Clarify what “update speed” measures.
items.because: Compression and download resumption may improve different measures.

items.says: State the test rig’s effect beyond the number of tests, if it can be substantiated.
items.because: The line establishes scale but not the result.

items.says: Say that the logged data helped diagnose the five failures.
items.because: A logger alone does not find root causes.

items.says: Sampling a 5 kHz signal at 8 kHz does not by itself prevent aliasing.
items.because: The Nyquist rate would be greater than 10 kHz.

items.says: Declaring the shared counter volatile does not by itself fix the race.
items.because: Volatile does not make access atomic or resolve a race between an interrupt and the main loop.

items.says: Move the motor-controller rewrite bullet near the top.
items.because: Its fleet scale and outcomes make it one of the strongest bullets.

items.says: Clarify whether the complaint counts compare equivalent quarterly periods.
Clarify whether the decline in complaints can reasonably be attributed to the procedure.
Be prepared to explain why the eight-board fixture raised throughput from 40 to 150 boards an hour rather than more.
items.because: Other bottlenecks may make that increase reasonable.

items.says: Remove the promotional language.
items.because: It says little about what was built and clashes with the concrete engineering detail elsewhere.

items.says: Specify the operating conditions behind the average-current comparison if they matter.
items.because: They may affect how the comparison is interpreted.

items.says: Check that the published work is accessible through the code link.
The warehouse robot fleet appears to belong to the robotics job, not the Formula Student project.
Make your own contribution to the CAN-bus firmware clear.
items.because: The passive wording obscures what you did.

items.says: Make the testing outcome clear.
The robot-fleet achievement duplicates the Voltline bullet with slightly different figures under a 2019–2021 project.
items.because: The discrepancy could undermine confidence in the whole résumé.

items.says: Separate languages, hardware and platforms, tools, and methods more accurately.
items.because: STM32 is a platform, while FPGA is not a tool in the same sense as an oscilloscope.

items.says: Include FPGA only if you can discuss relevant hands-on work.
Reflect any relevant work or projects since the Voltline role ended in June 2025.
